issue_context.title: udev: watch handle may be deleted by other devices
issue_context.body:
**systemd version the issue has been seen with**
 > 247

**Expected behaviour you didn't see**
 > Each disk or lvm device has a watch handle symlink in /run/udev/watch

**Unexpected behaviour you saw**
 > Some devices have no watch handle

**Steps to reproduce the problem**
 > The follow scripts can reproduce the problem
```
watch_org=$(ls -l /run/udev/watch | wc -l)

while true
do
        systemctl restart systemd-udevd
        sleep 3

        udevadm trigger
        udevadm settle
        watch_current=$(ls -l /run/udev/watch | wc -l)
        if [ $watch_org != $watch_current ]; then
                break
        fi
done
```
comments:
This is because it restore the watch handles in "systemctl restart systemd-udevd", but it not update the new info into db. And the problem is occured like follow(dx means device x, wdx -> dy means there has a symlink x->dy, dbx: y means device x's recorded watch handle is y in db):
1. wd4->d1(db1: 4) wd5->d2(db2: 5) wd6->d3(db3: 6)
2. After "systemctl restart systemd-udevd", the infos may like this:
    wd1->d1(db1: 4) wd2->d2(db2: 5) wd3->d3(db3: 6)
3. Trigger change event for d2, the infos will change to this:
    wd1->d1(db1: 4) wd4->d2(db2: 4) wd3->d3(db3: 6)
4. Trigger change event for d1, the problem will occur:
    "change event for d1" calls udev_watch_end to delete wd4, but at this time, wd4 is for d2.

PR https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/18524 can solve this problem.
@yuwata @poettering How about this issue? Is the solution gave in PR https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/18524 ok? Or we must find another solution?

@yuwata 
What else can I do about this issue?
I think https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/18524 is a better solution. The symlink in /run/udev/watch can save watch infos. So I think there's no need to write watch infos to db. And watch infos saved in two places may casue inconsistency.

Based on PR https://github.com/systemd/systemd/pull/18524, watch infos in db seems no use, if the PR is ok, I can cleanup related codes.
Sorry for late review. I will take a look.

review_comments: hmm, why is the IN_IGNORED handling dropped?

When `IN_IGNORED` is triggered, the corresponding 'remove' uevent for the device will be triggered, and during the process of the uevent, `udev_watch_end()` is called. So, it is not necessary to handle the flag here. Moreover, when both `udev_watch_end()` is called by both the main and worker process, then `device_remove_watch_handle()` in `udev_watch_end()` may cause some race. With this commit, `udev_watch_begin()` and `udev_watch_end()` are only called by workers. So, there should be no race.

I added short comment about that in the code.
maybe add comment here: `/* refuse duplicate slashes */` or so? because that's what this is supposed to do, no?
hmm, this has quite some potential of surfacing issues that noone noticed before because we ignore the results of remove rules, no?

When, some remove rules are failed, then this commit changes only two things: warn the failure, and skip `udev_event_execute_run()`. Skipping `udev_event_execute_run()` on some failure should be safer, as the execution list may be different from expected.
